short: Impact of crystallography at Ni/NiAl interfaces on the nucle
title: Impact of crystallography at Ni/NiAl interfaces on the nucleation of Ni3Al

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Whether interface crystallography at (Ni)/NiAl interfaces governs Ni3Al nucleation is unknown; orientation relationships undocumented in bulk diffusion couples. Interface crystallography, through interfacial and strain energies, should affect where and in which orientation Ni3Al nucleates.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/method), n5 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Reaction zone between NiAl and pure (Ni): a ~20-25 at% Al layer (Ni3Al) over a ~5 at% Al layer (Al-enriched (Ni)). Ni3Al on the NiAl side forms a thicker layer (1.35 um) than on the (Ni) side (0.5 um).

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Thickness of all three layers grows linearly with sqrt(t) at 650 C (parabolic growth). Layer growth at 650 C is diffusion-controlled.
states.detail: Absorbed: n8 (PRP/diagnostic), n10 (MEC/identification), n25 (MEC/pathway), n9 (PRP/value), n12 (MEC/pathway), n16 (PRP/value), n23 (PRP/value), n17 (MEC/pathway), n21 (PRP/value). Premises: Layer thickness proportional to sqrt(t) indicates diffusion-controlled growth; Interdiffusion coefficient in NiAl is ~10x that in (Ni); in Ni3Al it is higher at the NiAl side [8,45-48]; In Ni3Al of NiAl/(Ni) couples at 1000 C the intrinsic diffusivity of Ni is ~5x that of Al [34]; Heterogeneous nucleation: a nucleus in a low-energy orientation relationship has lower interfacial and strain energy, hence a lower barrier

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Ni3Al forms at (Ni)/NiAl by oriented nucleation sensitive to interface crystallography, followed by diffusion-controlled, asymmetric layer growth

nodes.title: evidence, F1
nodes.head: Al drops abruptly (~48 to ~25 at%) at the NiAl/Ni3Al boundary but declines gradually over ~0.7 um at the Ni3Al/(Ni) side
nodes.solves: Steeper concentration gradients and ~10x higher interdiffusivity on the NiAl side give a larger flux across the NiAl/Ni3Al interface, which migrates faster
nodes.detail: o2: Al drops abruptly (~48 to ~25 at%) at the NiAl/Ni3Al boundary but declines gradually over ~0.7 um at the Ni3Al/(Ni) side

nodes.title: EBSD, F2
nodes.head: Thickness of all three layers rises roughly linearly with sqrt(t) from 1 to 48 h. Ni3Al-into-(Ni) thickness at 48 h (~2.0 um) sits below its fit line (~2.2) and barely above 18 h (~1.7 um)
nodes.solves: Thickness of all three layers grows linearly with sqrt(t) at 650 C (parabolic growth)
nodes.op: fit model, read characteristic point, read trend
nodes.note: fits drawn through the origin (dashed extrapolation), so incubation cannot be resolved (paper says so); instrument for thickness not named, EBSD maps per F1 linked text; large error bars at 48 h suggests this layer slows beyond parabolic at long times; error bar ~1.4-2.6 um overlaps the line

nodes.head: Grain-size histograms at low and high nucleation interfaces both peak near 0.35 um; the high set has more 0.6-0.8 um grains and a tail to ~2.7 um
